newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MARCONS PLANS CAPITAL RESTRUCTURE.
newsitem.headline: MARCONS PLANS CAPITAL RESTRUCTURE.

text.p: Property firm Marshalls Controlling Investments Ltd (Marcons) said on Tuesday its board had decided to implement a capital restructuring.

The restructuring was aimed at improving the tradeability of its shares and helping it achieve a flexible structure which would enable it to take advantage of future growth prospects without affecting its voting control.
It said the proposal would be achieved by:
- the conversion of ordinary shares of one cent each into "N" shares of one cent each;
- an increase in authorised share capital by way of the creation of new ordinary shares of 100 cents each;
- a consolidation of its issued share capital; and
- a capitalisation issue of ordinary shares of 100 cents each.

Subject to shareholder approval, shareholders currently holding 100 shares of one cent each would hold 90 new ordinary shares of 100 cents each and ten "N" ordinary shares of one cent each after the restructuring.
The restructuring would also facilitate the removal of the group's pyramid structure, it said.

This would be achieved through a conditional offer by Marcons to ordinary shareholders of Marshalls Ltd to acquire all of their ordinary shares of no par value on the basis of 180 new Marcons "N" shares of one cent each and 20 new Marcons ordinary shares of 100 cents each for every 100 Marshall shares of no par value held.
Marcons holds a 69 percent stake in Marshalls.
A further announcement was expected to be made around September 15, the company said.
